title: Shelter After the Ruin
overview: After the disaster warned of in the previous chapter, Isaiah pictures a small group of survivors in Jerusalem made clean and sheltered by God's presence.

parts.label: Too few men left (v. 1)
parts.note: This finishes chapter 3's warning that Jerusalem's men will die in war, leaving so few that seven women plead with one man. They even give up the food and clothing a husband was expected to provide, just to bear his name and escape the shame of being unmarried.

parts.label: The Branch of the LORD (v. 2)
parts.note: The word pictures something sprouting and growing, and the survivors are promised a land that is fruitful and honored again. Scholars are unsure whether it means the land's renewed growth or a coming king, as the word means elsewhere in the Bible; Christians have read it as pointing to Jesus.

parts.label: A holy group of survivors (v. 3)
parts.note: Those who come through the disaster will be set apart as belonging to God. "Recorded among the living" likely draws on the family registers where the names of the living were kept.

parts.label: Washed by judgment and fire (v. 4)
parts.note: The "filth" looks back to the proud women of chapter 3, and the bloodstains to the violence and injustice condemned in chapter 1. God's judgment is pictured as fire that burns away what is wrong and leaves the city clean.

parts.label: Cloud by day, fire by night (vv. 5-6)
parts.note: This recalls the cloud and fire that led Israel out of Egypt as a sign that God was with them. Now that presence spreads over the whole city like a canopy, giving shade from the heat of the day and shelter from storm and rain.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether this promise was fulfilled in Jerusalem's recovery after exile, points mainly to Jesus and the church, or still awaits a future restored Jerusalem.
think: When a place or a person has been through real ruin, what do you think it takes for what remains to become something good rather than simply damaged?
